worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1-x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14069995/assets/782b4df0220d84d90d26a4ad1fd4a34da00ecf3c5d62a9416d9f0490ca765e2b.png)

From the description, the mass density function can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k{y}^{2},$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find an expression for $k$ in terms of $M$ by integrating the density function over the plate:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}k{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{1-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{3}(1-x)^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{3}{[-\frac{1}{4}(1-x)^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{k}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k=12M$ and hence $\lambda (x,y)=k{y}^{2}=12M{y}^{2}.$ Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{y}^{2}({y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1-x}{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{5}{y}^{5}]}_{0}^{1-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{5}(1-x)^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{12M}{5}{[-\frac{1}{6}(1-x)^{6}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{12M}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{2M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

  • The moment of inertia about the x-axis is given by Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the y-axis is given by Iy=∬Dx2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by I0=∬D(x2+y2)λ(x,y)dA=Ix+Iy.

First, notice that D is a type I region with representation D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤1−x},

as shown below.

From the description, the mass density function can be written as λ(x,y)=ky2, where k is a constant of proportionality. We can find an expression for k in terms of M by integrating the density function over the plate: M=∬Dλ(x,y)dA=∫01∫01−xky2dydx=k∫01[∫01−xy2dy]dx=k∫01[13y3]01−xdx=k∫0113(1−x)3dx=k3[−14(1−x)4]01=k3⋅14=k12

Therefore, k=12M and hence λ(x,y)=ky2=12My2. Therefore, the moment of inertia about the x-axis is

Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA=12M∫01∫01−xy2(y2)dydx=12M∫01[∫01−xy4dy]dx=12M∫01[15y5]01−xdx=12M∫0115(1−x)5dx=12M5[−16(1−x)6]01=12M5⋅16=2M5.
